evidence.observation: §4 PS3 requires "Reuse loaded snapshot indexes across ordered why-not targets." but the only §9 control is "PS3: replay two targets against one loaded snapshot and invalidate a negative witness when the blocked relation changes." Neither states that per-target answers computed against one shared loaded snapshot must equal answers from independent fresh-snapshot evaluations of the same targets, and the word "ordered" is never given semantics, so order-dependent memoization across targets would pass the stated acceptance pair.

concerns.recommendation: Add an explicit equivalence control to §9 PS3: for the two-target replay, assert each target's why-not result is byte-identical to a fresh per-target evaluation, and run the pair in both orders to exclude order-dependent cache effects.
concerns.title: PS3 shared-snapshot reuse has no equivalence control against independent evaluation

evidence.observation: §2 and §4 require a worker "with repeated requests, structured errors and model invalidation", but the §9 PS4 sequence is only "execute two requests in one isolated process, force one invalid input, then evaluate a valid request; log request IDs, model identities and restart behavior." No step invalidates a model, logging identities is not an assertion, and no expected post-invalidation outcome (reload and answer identically to a fresh worker, versus a structured refusal, versus mandated restart) is defined anywhere.

concerns.recommendation: Define the invalidation trigger (e.g. snapshot digest or model version change) and the required worker behavior, then extend the §9 sequence to force an invalidation and assert the chosen outcome; state the expected result of the valid request after the forced invalid input rather than only logging it.
concerns.title: PS4 model invalidation is a claimed deliverable but has no acceptance exercise or expected behavior

evidence.observation: §4 PS3's exit criterion includes "Report per-target work and exhaustion." but the §9 PS3 pair ("replay two targets against one loaded snapshot and invalidate a negative witness when the blocked relation changes") contains no exhaustion case, and the plan never defines exhaustion semantics: whether one exhausted target aborts the batch, is reported with a per-target status while the batch continues, or affects the shared index for later targets.

concerns.recommendation: Define per-target budget units and the exhaustion outcome in §4 or §6, and add a §9 fixture whose per-target budget is smaller than the required work, asserting the reported exhaustion status and the fate of the remaining targets.
concerns.title: PS3 per-target exhaustion is in the exit criterion but has no test and no defined semantics

evidence.observation: §4 PS2 promises results "from a single evaluation" and §9 prescribes "count evaluations, expecting one", but no evaluation counter, instrumentation point, or definition of what constitutes one evaluation (model load, checker pass, or api call) appears anywhere in the plan; §6's "Record work counters and the first refusal where limits apply" does not define the counters either, so two implementers can count different events and both claim compliance.

concerns.recommendation: Name the counter and its defining component in §9 (for example, invocations of the evaluation entry point in check.service), and state what activity must not increment it (index loads, disclosure formatting) so "expecting one" is falsifiable.
concerns.title: PS2 'single evaluation' claim rests on an evaluation counter the plan never defines

evidence.observation: §4 PS2 requires "disclosure and size limits" and to "Distinguish a complete empty extension from one that could not be computed", and §9 says "Exercise a redacted role and a capped extension" without asserting anything about the capped result. The plan never states cap units (rows or bytes), whether hitting the cap truncates or refuses, whether redacted rows count against the cap, or whether a capped extension must carry an incomplete marker; §6's "first refusal where limits apply" suggests refusal while a "capped extension" suggests partial rows, and a truncated result indistinguishable from a complete one would violate the phase's own distinction claim.

concerns.recommendation: Specify in §4 or §6 that a cap-hit extension is returned with an explicit incomplete/capped indicator (or refused), define the cap unit and the redaction interaction, and make the §9 capped-extension case assert the indicator and the exact row count.
concerns.title: PS2 capped-extension semantics (units, truncation vs refusal, completeness marker) are unspecified

evidence.observation: §4 PS3 states "Replay a fully grounded negative premise only with covered relations." but neither "fully grounded" nor "covered relations" is defined — coverage relative to the loaded snapshot's inventory, to declared relations, or to the witness's named relations is unstated — and the §9 pair exercises only the invalidation side ("invalidate a negative witness when the blocked relation changes"), leaving the positive replay condition untestable as written.

concerns.recommendation: Define covered relations (for example, relations present in the loaded snapshot's inventory) and full grounding in §4 or the PS3 spec, and add a positive §9 case where a grounded premise over a covered relation replays and one over an uncovered relation is refused.
concerns.title: PS3 'fully grounded negative premise' and 'covered relations' lack definitions

evidence.observation: §4 PS2 requires returning "availability" and distinguishing "a complete empty extension from one that could not be computed", but §10's only response-contract decision is "Approve the accessor name, response fields and unsupported-schema status", which §6 of the PS1 spec ties to api.snapshot_verdict; no open decision or later-spec commitment owns PS2's availability values or the representation of the empty-versus-uncomputed distinction (status enum, null versus empty rows), so the central PS2 contract can reach implementation undecided.

concerns.recommendation: Add a PS2 response-contract decision to §10 (availability enumeration and the empty/uncomputed encoding) and require it resolved before PS2 implementation, mirroring the PS1 rule.
concerns.title: PS2 availability values and the empty-vs-uncomputed representation have no owner decision

evidence.observation: §4 PS4 requires testing "shared dependency ranges against pinned builds and an independent host", while §9 makes "Lockfile reproducibility and shared-host installation" the separate gates; an independent host and a shared-host installation name different topologies, neither is defined (separate machine, container, or fresh virtualenv), and the plan does not map either gate to the §4 criterion, so the exit criterion is not evaluable as written.

concerns.recommendation: Define the host topologies in §4 or §10's dependency-test-matrix decision, state whether PS4 requires one or both, and align the §9 gate names with the criterion wording.
concerns.title: PS4 'independent host' criterion versus 'shared-host installation' gate is unreconciled

evidence.observation: §2 and §4 PS1 commit to "Normalize the supported snapshot envelopes" but the plan never enumerates the supported set; the only schema numbers appear as an intake observation ("The issue fixtures exercise raw schemas 7, 12 and 14") about fixture coverage, not as a support commitment, wrapper shapes are never mentioned at plan level, and the unsupported-schema status remains an open §10 decision, so the exit criterion cannot be checked without outside knowledge.

concerns.recommendation: Enumerate the supported schema versions and wrapper shapes in §4 PS1 (or bind them to the spec's list) and add an unknown-schema fixture asserting the chosen unsupported status, per the already-planned §10 decision.
concerns.title: PS1 never commits to a supported envelope inventory

evidence.observation: §2 requires "a versioned persistent local worker" and §3 says "the worker protocol freezes after the result and explanation contracts", but no version-negotiation or version-mismatch behavior is specified — a worker receiving a request at an unsupported protocol version has no stated outcome (structured error, refusal, upgrade) — and §10 defers only the transport, not versioning semantics.

concerns.recommendation: State the version-mismatch behavior alongside the transport decision in §10 and include a mismatched-version request in the §9 PS4 sequence with an asserted structured error.
concerns.title: Versioned worker protocol lacks a stated version-mismatch behavior

evidence.observation: The PS1 exit criterion ends "Document inventory-grounded participation with empty and missing coverage." — a documentation-only requirement for what is a behavioral distinction (empty coverage accepted versus missing coverage rejected), so a build with correct docs and inverted behavior satisfies the milestone-level criterion; only the PS1 spec's §8 ("the grounded inventory still fails on missing outcomes") supplies the behavioral assertion, and §4 is what milestone closure replays.

concerns.recommendation: Reword the §4 PS1 criterion to require the behavior (empty coverage participates, missing coverage fails) with documentation as the delivery vehicle, so the criterion remains falsifiable at milestone close.
concerns.title: PS1 criterion makes the empty-vs-missing coverage distinction documentation-only

evidence.observation: The §4 column is headed "Observable exit criterion" but each row restates the §2 deliverable (for example PS2's row repeats "Return requested derived rows, availability and findings from a single evaluation, with disclosure and size limits."), while §9 then instructs "use the issue reproduction and the criterion in §4 as an acceptance pair", pairing reproductions against text that contains no observable threshold; the actual observable conditions live scattered in §9 lines 59–60.

concerns.recommendation: Either retitle the column to match its content or move the §9 observable conditions (exit codes, expected counts, asserted statuses) into the §4 rows so the acceptance pair references genuinely observable criteria.
concerns.title: §4 'Observable exit criterion' column restates deliverables rather than stating observables

evidence.observation: §10 lists three PS1-scoped items in one sentence — "Approve the accessor name, response fields and unsupported-schema status." — then a PS4 item, then instructs "Resolve the first-phase decision before implementation"; the singular "decision" has no unambiguous antecedent among the three PS1 items, leaving it unclear whether all three or only one gate PS1 implementation.

concerns.recommendation: Enumerate the open decisions (D1 accessor name, D2 response fields, D3 unsupported-schema status, D4 worker transport and matrix) and state explicitly which identifiers must be resolved before PS1 implementation.
concerns.title: §10 'the first-phase decision' is ambiguous among the three listed PS1 decisions

response.summary: Plan r1 for python-snapshot-evaluation is structurally sound and its intake claims check out (the Pydantic 2.13.4 pin matches pyproject.toml:27, and the referenced PS1 spec and predecessor close exist). However, four of its own §4 exit criteria are not demonstrable under the §9 verification pairs: PS3 never asserts shared-index results equal independent evaluations, PS3 claims exhaustion reporting with no exhaustion case, PS2's single-evaluation claim relies on an undefined counter, and PS4 claims model invalidation that its acceptance sequence never exercises. A further set of hardening gaps leaves key terms (fully grounded, covered relations, cap semantics, availability values, independent host, supported envelope set) undefined at the plan level.
